case_title: Sangappa & Ors. v. State of Karnataka
high_court_outcome: Convicted under s. 304 (Part-II) read with s. 34 IPC
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that four individuals, referred to as the accused, murdered the deceased while he was working in a field. The deceased was involved in a dispute with the accused over a bullock that had strayed into their field. The accused became enraged and attacked the deceased, with one of them using a knife and others hitting him with stones. The deceased's father and mother were present at the scene but were pushed aside by the accused. The police registered a case based on the first information report, and the accused were arrested. The trial court acquitted the accused, finding the prosecution failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt. The High Court reversed the acquittal and convicted the accused under a different section of the IPC.
